records.name: Viking 2 lander
records.summary: Viking 2 landed at Utopia Planitia on September 3, 1976. Its stationary lander studied the surface and atmosphere.

details.purpose: Study Martian soil, weather and possible biological activity. Its biology results did not establish life.
details.operation: Cameras, a sampling arm, weather instruments and a laboratory supported surface science. Two RTGs supplied electricity.
details.discovery: The biology results were inconclusive, rather than a confirmed discovery of living organisms.
details.ending: The lander stopped communicating in April 1980. Its separate orbiter had ended operations in 1978.
details.location: Utopia Planitia, Mars; this identifies the surface lander, not its orbiter.
details.arrival: Viking 2 landed at Utopia Planitia on September 3, 1976. Its stationary lander studied the surface and atmosphere.

records.name: Mars Pathfinder lander
records.summary: Mars Pathfinder landed at Ares Vallis on July 4, 1997, delivering the Sojourner rover.

details.purpose: Demonstrate a lander and rover on Mars and investigate rocks, soil and weather.
details.operation: Airbags cushioned landing. The lander carried imaging and weather instruments.
details.discovery: Rock and soil observations supported investigation of a warmer, wetter Martian past.
details.ending: Its final data transmission was September 27, 1997.
details.location: Ares Vallis, Mars. The lander and Sojourner are separate artifacts.
details.arrival: Mars Pathfinder landed at Ares Vallis on July 4, 1997, delivering the Sojourner rover.

records.name: Sojourner rover
records.summary: Sojourner was the small rover delivered by Mars Pathfinder in July 1997.

details.purpose: Demonstrate a mobile robotic rover and investigate rocks and soil.
details.operation: Cameras and an alpha proton X-ray spectrometer supported imaging and elemental analysis.
details.discovery: The joint mission gathered geological and weather evidence about an ancient watery environment, not confirmed life.
details.ending: Pathfinder’s final transmission was September 27, 1997. This is not a live report of Sojourner’s condition.
details.location: Ares Vallis, Mars, near the Pathfinder lander.
details.arrival: Sojourner was the small rover delivered by Mars Pathfinder in July 1997.

records.name: Mars Polar Lander
records.summary: Mars Polar Lander was lost on arrival at Mars on December 3, 1999.

details.purpose: Investigate the south polar environment and dig for water ice with a robotic arm.
details.operation: A robotic arm and science instruments were intended for surface investigation; the planned surface work did not occur.
details.ending: The lander was lost during arrival. NASA ended attempts to contact it in January 2000.
details.location: The intended destination was near the south polar cap. This record does not provide a confirmed resting location.
details.arrival: Mars Polar Lander was lost on arrival at Mars on December 3, 1999.

records.name: Deep Space 2 probes
records.summary: Two experimental Deep Space 2 probes accompanied Mars Polar Lander and were lost on arrival in December 1999.

details.purpose: Test small probes intended to penetrate the Martian surface on impact.
details.operation: They were impact probes, separate from the main lander.
details.ending: No successful surface science return was established after arrival.
details.location: Their precise resting locations are not confirmed in this mission record.
details.arrival: Two experimental Deep Space 2 probes accompanied Mars Polar Lander and were lost on arrival in December 1999.

records.name: Ingenuity Mars Helicopter
records.summary: Ingenuity demonstrated powered, controlled flight on Mars and completed 72 flights.

details.purpose: Demonstrate powered flight on another planet, later helping scout terrain.
details.operation: Its solar panel charged batteries used for flight.
details.discovery: It demonstrated that controlled powered flight is possible in the thin Martian atmosphere.
details.ending: Its final flight was January 18, 2024. NASA announced the end of the flight mission January 25 after rotor damage. Flight retirement does not by itself mean every electronic system immediately stopped.
details.location: Jezero crater, Mars. This is a mission region, not a live position report.
